extracted.intended_audience: prospective Frontiers authors, reviewers, and handling editors
extracted.subtask_description: Describes Frontiers' end-to-end peer review workflow and the quality/ethical criteria used to evaluate submitted manuscripts, including initial checks, editorial assignment, independent review using the VALID criteria, an interactive review phase, final validation, and publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial validation (pre-screening)
rubrics_metrics.description: When you submit your manuscript it goes through a pre-screening process conducted by the research integrity team, supported by AIRA. These initial checks ensure the manuscript meets quality standards and adheres to ethical guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks look for: originality and potential plagiarism; adherence to ethical research practices; wider patterns of misconduct (such as organizational fraud); proper formatting and completeness of the submission. If the manuscript passes, it moves on to the next stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIRA checks (AI review assistant)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIRA supports the peer review team by identifying and resolving potential issues before and during peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AIRA assesses language quality, checks figure integrity, and identifies possible ethical concerns, providing clear and actionable feedback so authors can address areas early and potentially reduce revision time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial assignment and preliminary content check
rubrics_metrics.description: A handling editor from the relevant specialty section conducts a preliminary content check and decides whether to send the manuscript for peer review or recommend immediate rejection to the specialty chief editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the editor recommends rejection the specialty chief editor reviews and may confirm or override the rejection and/or assign a new handling editor. Manuscripts remain in this stage until a reviewer accepts an invitation to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and clarity as grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are sometimes rejected due to poor language quality or unclear writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are advised to address language/clarity issues before submission and ensure compliance with the author guidelines to improve chances of moving forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review reporting timeline and template
rubrics_metrics.description: Once reviewers accept the invitation they have 10 days to submit independent review reports using a standardized review template adapted to each article type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures consistent, thorough reviews across submissions. Reviewers may be from the board of review editors or recruited subject experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: VALID — Valid research question and hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: V: valid research question and hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on whether the study asks an appropriate, well-formulated research question and hypothesis supported by the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: VALID — Applies correct and transparent methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: A: applies correct and transparent methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether methods are appropriate, correctly applied, and transparently reported so results can be assessed and reproduced where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: VALID — Language and presentation are clear and adequate
rubrics_metrics.description: L: language and presentation are clear and adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates clarity of writing, organization, figures/tables, and overall presentation quality to ensure the research is understandable.

rubrics_metrics.name: VALID — In line with Frontiers' author guidelines and ethical policies
rubrics_metrics.description: I: manuscript complies with author guidelines and ethical policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers check adherence to journal-specific submission requirements and ethical standards (e.g., consent, approvals, disclosures).

rubrics_metrics.name: VALID — Determined by grounding in existing literature
rubrics_metrics.description: D: determined by a grounding in existing literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether the work is properly contextualized, cites relevant prior work, and situates contributions relative to existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recommendation categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submitting their report, reviewers can accept the paper as is, recommend minor revisions, major revisions, or recommend rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers recommend rejection the handling editor determines next steps and may activate the major concerns protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major concerns protocol (rebuttal opportunity)
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers recommend rejection and the handling editor supports rejection, the major concerns protocol is activated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors have seven days to submit an optional rebuttal. This does not guarantee continuation but provides a chance to respond or revise before a final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive review phase (collaborative dialogue)
rubrics_metrics.description: After all reviewers submit reports the handling editor activates the interactive review phase, allowing authors and reviewers to engage in direct dialogue via an online collaborative forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can view and respond to reviewers' comments; reviewers can clarify and ask follow-up questions; the handling editor moderates. Authors typically have 7–14 days to respond or submit a revised manuscript; extensions can be requested. When resubmitting, authors should provide a point-by-point reply to all reviewer comments; if Reviewer tab is closed they can reply in the Editor tab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-anonymized review model
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers operates a single-anonymized review model in which reviewers can see the authors’ names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows reviewers to provide a more informed assessment, helps identify potential conflicts of interest before accepting an invitation, and Frontiers publicly acknowledges endorsing reviewers once an article is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling editor finalization and minimum endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: At review finalization the handling editor reviews the paper to ensure it meets the journal’s standards and can choose to accept the manuscript once the minimum number of endorsements is met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers can recommend acceptance, revision or rejection at any time. The handling editor can recommend rejection to the specialty chief editor, who makes the final decision on rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: No target rejection rate; focus on validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers has no target rejection rate and focuses on publishing all valid research that meets quality standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes objectivity and prioritizing validity and quality over perceived impact; encourages open science and accessibility of credible research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final validation by peer review specialists and chief editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Before publication, peer review specialists and the journal's chief editors conduct a final assessment to confirm the manuscript meets standards for quality and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief editors ensure each manuscript aligns with high standards and makes a meaningful contribution to the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication contingent on APC payment and production processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the manuscript has passed final validation and the article publishing charge has been paid, it is passed to the production team for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of the APC is a required step before production and final publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency as a guiding principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency: names of handling editors and reviewers are published on final articles to promote accountability and recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice is presented as a quality pillar that promotes trust and reduces bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration as a guiding principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaboration: the interactive/construction review phase fosters direct dialogue among authors, reviewers, and editors to improve manuscripts efficiently and constructively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a unique feature that results in more efficient manuscript improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness as a guiding principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness: Frontiers aims for a streamlined process with an average review time under 90 days for many journals/sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stresses efficiency supported by teams and AIRA to reduce turnaround times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous quality control and research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigorous quality control: multi-layered approach including editorial checks, peer review, and final validation managed by a large research integrity team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to protect communities and safeguard the scientific record; presented as a major differentiator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for reviewers (Frontiers Discover)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for reviewers: Frontiers Discover enables review editors to browse submitted manuscripts and volunteer to review those matching their expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to help ensure the right expertise evaluates each paper and to facilitate reviewer recruitment.
